IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Monday, October 5, 2026**

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** is sitting on 127 calls with nearly 1,000 hands available—the board's drowning in bodies. Miller Electrical and Inglett & Stubbs are running the QTS Fayetteville data center hall build with conduit and cable tray work at **$42/hr**. It's steady work but the depth is brutal; don't expect quick dispatch out of this one unless you land early.

**LU-583 El Paso, TX** is the pay-play if you've got mobility. Cupertino's Santa Teresa job hits **$70/hr** with a fat **$1121.00 per week per diem** for the 350+ mile move—that's serious money for NM State JIW licensed hands. You'll need OSHA 10 and a clean test, but the math works. Coltrane's Meta El Paso sit is **$45** with a tighter **$100/day** PD.

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** has 55 calls chasing 301 hands on the Port Washington Data Center jobs—Cupertino and Gurtz Electric both offering JW wage plus **$10/hr base wage increase** on top. That's over-scale movement and they're still filling. Tight board, steady project.

**LU-405 Cedar Rapids, IA** is burning through the EWD Data Center call—CST's running 42 JW slots on six 10s starting 7AM with **$10 over scale** per diem and **all OT double time**. OSHA 10 required. This is the kind of work density that moves fast; 68-hour weeks are live at QTS if you want the hours.

**LU-575 Portsmouth, OH** just posted fresh calls. TSC's North Campus Amazon job (Jeffersonville) starts *today* with 90 hands on 4-10s; Blattner's Palomino Solar Fields is 9 JW slots at **$100/day** PD on 5-8s. Both starting Monday.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** has Cache Valley running QTS and Facebook with **$46.22** base, **$10–$20 over scale per diem**, and solid scheduling (5-10s, some Saturdays). Smaller board but clean work.

Data center buildouts are still the gravity well—Milwaukee, Cedar Rapids, and Salt Lake are moving volume. El Paso pays the premium but requires licensed mobility.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Monday, October 5, 2026**

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is the board to watch this week—18 calls, 57 hands needed, and the money is there. FAITH ELECTRIC's running 10 Journeyman spots in College Park/Columbus on distribution at **$49.8/hr** plus **$150/day** per diem, 4-10s with hotels covered. But the real play is SERVICE ELECTRIC's Georgia Transmission work in Social Circle: one call hits **$56.8/hr** (local scale +$10) with Quanta barehand cert required; another pays **$46.8/hr** with 11-on-3-off hitch work and 2+ years transmission experience. W2 ENERGY SERVICES is also staffing five spots on reconduct/conversion at **$46.8/hr**, Wednesday-Wednesday 8-on-6-off. Deep board, solid contractors, transmission and distribution both live.

**LU-1393 Indianapolis, IN** sits at 9 calls, 13 hands, and P&G Power is headlining with four Journeyman spots in Goshen at **$67.18/hr** plus **$100/day** per diem—69kv with 12kv underbuild, pole sets and wire pull. Thayer and Michels are also staffing South Bend/Elkhart and Fort Wayne transmission. This is strong-pay work for the Midwest.

**LU-245 Toledo, OH** has five calls chasing 13 hands—all transmission and distribution through DIDADO and KENT POWER. DIDADO's Oak Harbor and Sandusky runs are showing **$58.03/hr** with **$225/day** per diem and CDL-A requirement. Hitch work territory.

**LU-17 Southfield, MI** — three calls, 16 hands. Lecom, OHL, and Thayer are all running distribution and streetlights work at **$58.97/hr**, **$100/day** per diem where you qualify (100+ miles from showup). Clean board, one foreman slot available.

**LU-602 Amarillo, TX** — 3 calls, 11 hands. HEARTLAND ELECTRIC is running 8 Inside JW in Amarillo proper at **$50/hr**, 6-10s. DACON's Gale and Afton work pays **$53.72/hr** and **$40.23/hr** respectively with **$150/day** per diem and 6-10s schedules.

**LU-583 El Paso, TX** — tight board but hot: B&D Industries' Santa Teresa, New Mexico project is **$70/hr** fire-alarm-focused work, while Mass Electric on the same site runs **$55/hr** all-OT-double-time. Both require NM State JIW License EE98J.

The work is flowing south and midwest—transmission buildout and data-center infrastructure are pulling hands hard into Texas, Indiana, and Ohio.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Wednesday, September 30, 2026**

**LU-776 Lima, OH** is running hot with 7 calls across 44 hands—the board's biggest play right now. Gem's got 10 combo welders headed to the fab shop (7-10s, will test you); Graham needs 4 pipefitters on Cenovus maintenance work (6-10s, spotty OT); Nooter's pushing 5 more pipefitters into the Cenovus fab shop with **$125/day** per diem and incentive pay, but you're getting current in DISA first. The other Gem call (BDO fab shop, 2 fitters, 7-10s) requires current status upfront. This is steady industrial maintenance and fab work—the kind that sticks around.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** has 5 calls, 20 hands available. The standout: Kiewit's posting 1 CWI slot at **$65** per diem (also **$65** base mentioned), night shift with **15% shift differential**, 5/10s schedule. Power Source Services wants 5 combo welders with rigging cert or rigging experience for JM Shafer Station in Fort Lupton. US Eng. Metalworks needs 2 fitters with SS fitting experience on night shift shop work. Trautman and Shreve's fab shop (3 combo welders, MIG/TIG focus) splits day and swing. Strong specialized work.

**LU-213 St John, NB** is thin—2 calls, 3 hands total—but strategic. Stuart Olson's Irving Oil Refinery call wants F3/F4 welders who can test F3/F4, starting ASAP at 7:30pm. The other call is a journeyman pipefitter into Lorneville LNG (4x10s plus, Industrial Agreement rate). Refinery and LNG infrastructure: good hold if you clear the testing.

**LU-192 Cheyenne, WY** has 1 call for 2 hands: PMI's Fort Meade VA Hospital job in Sturgis, South Dakota needs a plumber with med gas, OSHA10, and background clearance. **$100/day** per diem for days worked. Federal work, solid.

**LU-325 Fredericton, NB** shows 1 call: HVAC Inc.'s Moncton Fisheries Science Building needs a journeyman plumber, day shift (7 a.m.), 5-8s. Light board, tight timeline.

The industrial refinery and fab work is pulling hands east and south; LNG and power infrastructure keeps the momentum west.
